Batches from Arrow streams

Source: R/arrow.R
zl_arrow_batches.Rd

zl_arrow_batches() reads record batches from an Arrow stream, such as a 'DuckDB' query, a Parquet file or an 'arrow' table, and cuts them into batches of exactly rows rows for zl_step() and zl_forward(), which take the iterator as data. zl_next() returns the next batch as R arrays, for inspection. Each batch is one copy of the data: columns are interleaved into feature-major arrays, c(features, rows).

Usage

zl_arrow_batches(
  stream,
  map,
  rows,
  na = c("error", "mask"),
  last = c("drop", "pad")
)

zl_next(it)

# S3 method for class 'zl_arrow_batches'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

stream

An Arrow stream: a nanoarrow_array_stream, or an object that 'nanoarrow' converts to one (a data frame, an 'arrow' table or reader).

map

A named list from input names to column names, as above.

rows

The rows per batch.

na

What a missing value does: "error" or "mask".

last

What the final, partial batch does: "drop" or "pad".

it

An iterator from zl_arrow_batches().

x

An iterator, for print().

...

Unused.

Value

zl_arrow_batches() returns an iterator of class zl_arrow_batches; zl_next() a named list of arrays, or NULL at the end of the stream.

Details

map names the graph's inputs and gives each its columns: a character vector for an f32 input of c(length(columns), rows), or zl_int(...) around the column names for an i32 input (a vector of rows for one column). float32 columns are copied, float64 rounded to f32, int8 to int64 and boolean (0 and 1) go to either kind of input, and dictionary-encoded columns of strings go to i32 inputs as their codes, counting from 0. int64 values beyond the 32-bit range are errors in an i32 input. The dictionary must be the same in every record batch. Other types are refused.

Missing values are errors naming the column and row (na = "error"). With na = "mask" they are written as 0, and every input x gets a companion input x_mask of its shape holding 1 for a value and 0 for a missing one. The rows left at the end of the stream are dropped (last = "drop"), or padded with zeros to a full batch (last = "pad"), in which case every batch carries a row_mask input of rows values, 1 for a real row and 0 for padding. A graph that takes the iterator declares these inputs too.

The stream is taken over by the iterator: it is read on the main thread only, as producers such as 'DuckDB' require, and released when it ends or when the iterator is garbage collected. zl_step() and zl_forward() return NULL once it has ended.

A nanoarrow_array_stream is used directly; anything else is converted with nanoarrow::as_nanoarrow_array_stream(), which needs the 'nanoarrow' package (a zulm_companion_error without it).

Examples

if (requireNamespace("nanoarrow", quietly = TRUE)) {
  df <- data.frame(a = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5), b = c(0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5),
                   kind = factor(c("x", "y", "x", "x", "y")))
  it <- zl_arrow_batches(df, list(x = c("a", "b"), kind = zl_int("kind")), rows = 2)
  zl_next(it)
  zl_next(it)
  zl_next(it)
}
#> NULL
